content.content:
**Free plan limits:**

- **Projects:** Up to 2 active projects. You can have more paused projects.
- **Pausing:** Inactive projects pause after 1 week.
- **Database size:** 500 MB, on shared CPU with 500 MB RAM.
- **Monthly active users (MAU):** 50,000.
- **Egress:** 5 GB, plus 5 GB of cached egress.
- **File storage:** 1 GB, with a 50 MB maximum upload size.
- **API requests:** Unlimited.
- **Edge Function invocations:** 500,000.
- **Realtime:** 200 peak concurrent connections, 2 million messages per month, and 256 KB maximum message size.
- **Logs:** 1-day retention, 1 GB ingestion, and 100 GB query.
- **Auth audit logs:** Kept for 1 hour.
- **Image transformations:** Not included.
- **Automatic backups, point-in-time recovery, and branching:** Not included.
- **Custom domains and log drains:** Not included.
- **Support:** Community only. Email support is not included.

content.text:
As of today (2026-10-16), Neon and Supabase have free Postgres tiers and PlanetScale doesn't. I got each figure by fetching the vendor page named below. I didn't check the figures against anything else. The pricing pages change often, so check them again before you commit to a choice.

| | **Neon Free** | **Supabase Free** | **PlanetScale Postgres** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $0/month | $0/month | No free plan; the cheapest single-node option is $5/month |
| Storage | 1 GB per project, 20 GB across the account | 500 MB database | Extra storage is billed separately |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project, autoscaling up to 2 CU (8 GB RAM) | Shared CPU, 500 MB RAM | PS-5 single node at $5/month |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active (more can be paused) | Not applicable |
| Idle behaviour | Scales to zero after 5 minutes of inactivity, and this can't be turned off | Projects pause after 1 week of inactivity | Not applicable |
| Branching | 10 branches per project | Not included | Not stated on the page I fetched |
| Egress | 5 GB per project | 5 GB, plus 5 GB cached | Billed separately |
| Backups and restore | 6-hour history window, up to 1 GB-month of changes; 1 manual snapshot | No automatic backups or point-in-time recovery | Backups billed separately |
| Auth | 60,000 monthly active users | 50,000 monthly active users | Not stated |
| Other included extras | 5 GB object storage; 1M function invocations per project | 1 GB file storage; 500,000 Edge Function invocations; Realtime with 200 peak concurrent connections | Not stated |
| Support | Community | Community | Not stated |

**PlanetScale detail:**
- Its Postgres pricing is per SKU. The cheapest listed options are a single-node PS-5 at $5/month and a three-node high-availability PS-5 at $15/month.
- Metal high-availability starts at $50/month for 10 GiB of storage.
- These prices are for AWS us-east-1 and vary by cloud provider and region.
- The page says the cluster price excludes extra storage, backups, egress, dedicated PgBouncer, and replicas beyond the standard replication.
- The page I fetched didn't mention a free tier. That doesn't prove none exists elsewhere, but I found no evidence of one.

**Comparing the two free tiers:**
- Neon gives more database storage per project (1 GB against 500 MB) and allows many more projects (100 against 2).
- Neon also includes branching and a short restore window.
- Supabase bundles more of a backend platform (auth, file storage, Realtime, Edge Functions).
- Supabase pauses a project after a week of inactivity, so it suits an always-on small app less well.
- Neon's idle suspension is shorter (5 minutes) but wakes the database automatically on the next connection.

**Sources:**
- Neon: https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans. My first fetch of https://neon.com/pricing failed with a connection error, so all Neon figures come from the docs page.
- Supabase: https://supabase.com/pricing
- PlanetScale: https://planetscale.com/pricing
